claims.text: Wat Phra Kaew, most commonly known in English as the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, is widely regarded as the most sacred Buddhist temple in Thailand.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It is located entirely within the historic precincts of the Grand Palace and was specially built as a royal chapel, meaning it uniquely lacks living quarters for monks.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Construction began in 1783 under King Rama I, and its main hall became the very first building in the entire palace compound to be completed in masonry.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The temple solemnly enshrines the Emerald Buddha, a highly revered and flawless Buddha image that was meticulously carved from a single block of solid jade.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1785, this precious statue was transported with great ceremony from its former home at Wat Arun across the river and installed in its present position.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Inside the main hall, every wall is covered in stunning painted murals, including an eastern wall depicting the Buddha's dramatic battle against the demon Mara.
claims.subject: self
